item_definition.name: Telematics, OTA Update & ADAS Actuation Subsystem
item_definition.system_boundary: Includes the cellular, cabin Wi-Fi and physical maintenance interfaces on the Telematics Control Unit (TCU), internal Ethernet routing through the Central Gateway (CGW), and CAN-FD actuation commands to the Electronic Brake Control Module (EBCM). The in-vehicle ADAS controller is outside the item boundary and supplies AEB requests to the CGW.

functions.name: Over-the-Air (OTA) Firmware Update
functions.description: The TCU downloads firmware from the OEM cloud over the cellular link (CONN-01) and sends it to the CGW over CONN-03. A CGW update ends at the gateway. For an EBCM update, the gateway forwards the image over CONN-04 to the EBCM.

functions.name: Remote Diagnostics & Telemetry
functions.description: Collects vehicle health logs and GPS coordinates and transmits them to the OEM backend.

functions.name: Autonomous Emergency Braking (AEB) Request
functions.description: COMP-ADAS periodically sends the requested deceleration to COMP-CGW over CONN-05 while AEB is active. COMP-CGW relays each request once over CONN-04 to COMP-EBCM, which controls hydraulic braking.

components.name: Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) Controller
components.role: Uses forward-sensor information to decide when automatic emergency braking is needed and request a deceleration.

hosted_software.name: openssl
hosted_software.role: Provides TLS for the OTA agent connection to the OEM cloud on TCP port 443

hosted_software.name: wpa_supplicant
hosted_software.role: Manages the TCU cabin Wi-Fi access point

hosted_software.name: ota_agent_daemon
hosted_software.role: Downloads firmware to /tmp/ota_update.bin and forwards via DoIP to CGW

hosted_software.name: doip_uds_router
hosted_software.role: Routes Diagnostics over IP (DoIP) from Ethernet to CAN-FD buses

firmware_programming.authorization_rule: For its own firmware, COMP-CGW accepts the programming request only after it verifies the fixed programming credential held by the TCU OTA agent.

firmware_activation.on_check_failure: Reject activation of the candidate image

hosted_software.name: brake_torque_controller
hosted_software.role: Actuates hydraulic brake valves based on CAN ID 0x120 deceleration messages

operational_parameters.aeb_request_acceptance: Accept a correctly formatted request within the configured deceleration range. Apply its demand and record the local reception time. An accepted zero clears AEB demand immediately.
operational_parameters.aeb_request_timeout: Hold the last accepted demand until the configured interval since its reception expires. Rejected requests do not refresh the interval.
operational_parameters.aeb_on_timeout: Clear AEB demand only. Apply the next accepted request on receipt.

firmware_activation.on_check_failure: Reject activation of the candidate image

connections.name: Cellular OTA & Telemetry Link
connections.purpose: The TCU initiates HTTPS sessions to download OTA images and upload telemetry.
connections.authenticated: Server-only TLS (No mTLS client certificate authentication)

connections.name: Cabin Wi-Fi Access Point
connections.authenticated: WPA2 pre-shared key for Wi-Fi access

ssh_maintenance.authentication: Root login requires a workshop SSH key authorized on the TCU.

connections.name: In-Vehicle Automotive Ethernet Link
connections.authenticated: None (Plaintext TCP/IP without MACsec or IPsec)

connections.name: Chassis & Safety CAN-FD Bus
connections.protocol: Raw CAN Frames (ID 0x120) & UDS on CAN (ISO 15765-2)

connections.name: Physical TCU Maintenance Console
connections.medium: Physical service connection at the vehicle diagnostic connector
connections.authenticated: Physical connection required. The serial console requires no login credential.

damage_scenarios.description: Loss of gateway or brake ECU function can prevent emergency braking when needed. A resulting collision can cause serious injury or death. Loss of ECU function can also prevent vehicle use.
Spoofed braking commands trigger unintended emergency braking at highway speeds, or DoS flooding prevents legitimate braking.
Exfiltration of real-time vehicle location and driver behavior history via compromised TCU.
